name: project-init
description: v0.28.0: the hook-liveness probe learns the cloud case. Its first live run (2026-09-02) correctly reported NOT LOADED, and the cause was neither version nor install: cloud (Cowork) sessions fire SessionStart before synced plugins register their hooks, so gstack-execution 0.9.0 and ponytail 0.2.0 now deliver on the first user prompt. The probe accepts the block wherever it arrived (start or first prompt) and says which; the remedy ladder is re-ordered for that (refresh to ≥0.9.0 → reinstall on-computer / read /tmp/claude-preload.out in the cloud → wiring); the canonical checks path is corrected to skills/gstack-execution/references/verification-checks.md and the skill now says to read it in the same turn whenever the line is NOT LOADED. v0.26.0: fixes /init-project's 2+ repos instruction, which told the model to relabel a multi-repo project's GitHub section as 'GitHub repos — READ-ONLY' and retain a fabricated 'READ-ONLY rule' for every repo — directly contradicting the vault template's own multi-repo posture (READ/WRITE, same as single-repo) and the classic-PAT commit+push workflow every other project uses. Following that instruction literally would have generated a multi-repo project with no commit/push mechanics at all. Fixed to pluralize the section 3 heading to 'GitHub repos — READ/WRITE (if applicable)' and replace only the single-repo opening sentence with an enumerated repo list, while explicitly preserving every other word of the template's section 3 verbatim: the Reads-vs-Writes split, the classic-PAT Mechanics (PAT vault location, the no-token-leak per-URL auth header, git config user.email/user.name, the shallow-clone-to-/tmp note, plain-text commit authoring), the GitHub-Desktop-retired line, the team-shared-memory reminder, and the never-write-to-.git/ line. Audited the 5 existing multi-repo projects (Frontier Founder, OpenControls, GRCSchema, AI Scrape Safe, Nexus) against this bug -- none were actually affected (all correctly READ/WRITE with full commit+push mechanics already), so this is a forward-looking fix, not a repair. v0.25.0: fixes a data-loss bug in /init-project. It had no check for whether the resolved project already had saved Project Instructions, so re-running it on an already-initialized project (e.g. because the user asked to 'configure' or 'update' project instructions rather than literally typing /init-project) silently re-scaffolded from scratch — asking 'which project are we initializing' even when the project name was already known from context, and Step 3 would have overwritten the on-disk cowork-project-instructions.md, discarding any hand-written Project-Specific Overrides. Added a Step 0 guard: resolve the project from context first (same signals /session-start uses — explicit name, launch directory / mounted Taskade subfolder), check whether it already has saved instructions, and if so STOP and ask the user to run /refresh-project-instructions instead (default), view the current file, or explicitly confirm a destructive from-scratch regenerate. Only a genuinely new, not-yet-initialized project reaches the 'Project name' question and Step 3's write. Also tightened the skill's frontmatter/When-to-use description so 'configure/update/fix project instructions' phrasing about an already-running project routes to /refresh-project-instructions instead of triggering this skill. v0.24.0: fixes the stale 'mounting is a user-only action in the cloud' premise in the Folder access convention shared by /session-start, /session-end, and /init-project. mcp__remote-devices__device_request_folder_access lets Claude proactively request specific folder paths and get them mounted through a single user-approval dialog, entirely from the cloud session — the old flow only tried that after telling the user to click Add folder first. Auto-mount is now the default action, not a fallback: online, all currently-missing roots are requested in ONE device_request_folder_access call (one approval dialog covers every root); on-computer, request_cowork_directory is unchanged as the mount path. Falling back to asking the user to add a folder manually now happens only when the remote-devices bridge is unavailable (no connected device / tool absent) or the user declines the request. /session-start's Step 3 mount logic, its Step 5 briefing template's mount-status wording ('newly mounted (auto-requested)' vs 'already mounted'), and its edge-case note were all updated to match; /session-end's mounting-issues edge case and /init-project's Folder access convention got the same auto-mount-first treatment. Pairs with a same-day vault fix (Cowork Project Instructions Template.md and project-instructions-loader-stub.md D2 reconciliation directive) that carried the identical stale premise for project-instructions files — that vault fix covers what /refresh-project-instructions stamps into each project's on-disk instructions; this plugin update covers the skill procedure itself. v0.23.0: task-board reads moved from the retired vault kanban (KANBAN_VIEW.md) to the team Jira board (project MOXY). /session-start Step 4b now queries MOXY via the Atlassian MCP, strictly filtered to the project's Jira label (project-<slug>, mapped from the declared #project/<slug> scope), fail-closed; the 'Kanban project tag(s)' field now denotes a Jira label rather than a vault tag. Jira is the single canonical board org-wide (2026-07-16 migration). v0.22.0: folder access is now fully mode-agnostic across online (cloud) and offline (on-computer) Cowork. Instead of treating on-computer as a synonym for 'the request_cowork_directory tool exists', each capability is detected by tool presence with a filesystem-probe fallback: DETECT availability via get_device_info (online) or by listing the path directly (offline); MOUNT a missing root via request_cowork_directory when present, else prompt the user to Add folder (online: desktop app button; offline: Cowork -> Folders -> Add); PICK a subfolder via the native picker when present, else device_list_dir + AskUserQuestion chips. Nothing hard-depends on request_cowork_directory, so session-start/session-end/init-project run identically whether Cowork is online or offline. v0.21.0: folder mounting is now environment-aware. The old assumption that `mcp__cowork__request_cowork_directory` is always present held only on-computer; in the cloud that tool is absent. /session-start, /session-end, and /init-project now detect the environment by tool availability and branch: in the cloud they detect mounts via `mcp__remote-devices__get_device_info` (`connectedFolders`), prompt the user to click Add folder for any missing root (mounting is a user-only trust action in the cloud), and replace the Finder picker with `device_list_dir` + AskUserQuestion chips for subfolder selection; on-computer they keep the `request_cowork_directory` picker/mount path. v0.20.0: /session-start now surfaces the project MOC index (the durable map) and the Taskade project-memory.md pointer in its briefing, not just the last-14-day DRs. Cowork project lifecycle for MoxyWolf projects. /init-project scaffolds tailored Project Instructions. /session-start auto-resolves the project — explicit argument, then launch directory, then the most recently active project, never a picker — mounts the three standard roots, reads the previous session's handoff including the `author` / `for` baton-pass fields, and probes the team-shared OpenRouter key (DR-010). /session-end asks who authored the handoff and whether it's a baton-pass, writes the canonical handoff with `author` / `for` frontmatter, supports --author / --handoff-to / --solo, refreshes each writable repo's README.md, then runs /obsidian-update. v0.15.0 closes the stale-handoff-reminder propagation hole: /session-start now reads Taskade/_Shared Files/_shared-memory/INDEX.md as a first-class briefing step and cross-checks the handoff's procedural-reminders section against the current INDEX, flagging any reminder that cites a missing or revised file as STALE. /session-end now requires every general behavioral reminder in the procedural-reminders section to cite a currently-existing team-shared memory file by exact filename (verified at write time), or be explicitly tagged as (session-specific). Together the two checks stop free-form recollections from overriding canonical team-shared memory across sessions — the failure mode that surfaced 2026-06-02 when a 2026-05-21 handoff carried forward a 'never run git from the sandbox' reminder that had been reversed 2026-05-20. v0.16.0 moved commit+push to sandbox git + a classic PAT (no GitHub Desktop in the loop); v0.17.0 reads that PAT from the vault file github-pat.env (DR-011), mirroring the openrouter.env pattern, and verifies each push landed via git ls-remote. v0.18.0 switches /init-project to the loader-stub model: it saves the full instructions on disk as the single source of truth and emits only a thin loader stub (mounts + file-write-path override + a read-the-file-and-shared-memory-first imperative) for the Cowork settings field, so the embedded copy can no longer drift out of sync with the on-disk file (the paste-once-never-re-paste model; DR-010). v0.19.0 moves the stub skeleton and the on-disk reconciliation directives OUT of the plugin into a vault spec (MoxyWolf Vault/_Shared Knowledge/Agents and Plugins/project-instructions-loader-stub.md) that both /init-project and the new /refresh-project-instructions command read at run time, and adds /refresh-project-instructions to migrate or re-stamp an existing project from that spec — so changing a project-instruction rule is a vault edit plus a per-project command run, never a plugin update.
